item.text: I’m doing a second pass with a narrower design goal: separate the algorithm from the demo and make the selection API more explicit about mutation and indexing behavior.
I’m editing `quickselect.java` again. This pass will pull demo concerns out of the selector, preserve the current entrypoint, and isolate pivot selection so the partition step has a cleaner contract.

Refactored [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:3) again to make the design more explicit.

The main change is the API split at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:9): `selectKthSmallest` now guarantees non-mutating behavior by copying input, while `selectKthSmallestInPlace` makes the mutating path explicit. I kept `kthSmallest` as a compatibility wrapper. I also separated the demo into `QuickSelectDemo` at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:112), with `QuickSelect.main` delegating to preserve the existing entrypoint.

The partitioning logic is cleaner now because pivot selection is isolated behind a median-of-three helper at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:23). That reduces coupling inside `partition` and gives better default behavior than always choosing the last element.
